_hand: NEVER edited by hand. `--restamp` writes it: `node scripts/check-unit-count.mjs --restamp <vitest-report.json>` and `node scripts/check-pw-projects.mjs --restamp`. A hand-lowered floor REDs the band arm in both gates, which is the point.

law.derive: live <= exactAtOrBelow ? live : max(floor(live * churnRoom), ceil(live * band)) — a project of deliberate arity sits at its exact live count; a bigger one keeps ~10% of churn room, never so much that it falls out of the band. The max() closes the 11-and-12 hole: floor(11*0.9)=9 sits UNDER ceil(11*0.85)=10, so the plain churn rule would derive a floor its own band rejects.
law.band_rule: floor >= ceil(band * max(stampedCensus, live)). The band is held against whichever is HIGHER — the stamp or what the tree resolves right now — so it REDs in both directions: a census inflated above live REDs it (the stamp is a claim, not a wish), and an estate that grows past the floor without a restamp REDs it (silent slack growth, the disease). 0.85 buys ~17.6% of growth room before a restamp is compulsory.
law.ratchet: restamp takes max(banked, derived), so closing slack never hands any back and a restamp on an unmoved tree proposes NOTHING (it round-trips). Only when the derived floor would sit ABOVE live have tests actually left: that is a real LOWERING and needs --restamp --allow-lower "<where they went>".
law._why_ratchet: T7 blamed a data-loop miscount for the restamp arm's refusal. The true mechanism (V4, reproduced at HEAD): the arm derives its floors under a rule the banked floors were never authored under, so it proposed 14 -> 12 on both theme-quadrants projects, called that a LOWERING, and exited 1. The arm could not run at a WGATE without an --allow-lower saying tests had left when none had. check-coverage-floor.mjs already carries the max() ratchet for the identical problem (T7-W6 evidence, floor-restamp-mechanism.txt §2); this is that cure applied to the other two floors.
